title: world protocol — values
description: The scalar and addressing primitives every component is built out of: identities, references, derivation addresses, quantities with their units fixed by the field name, and the two annotation keys a document may carry. Mirrors the crate's ids.rs, derivation.rs and units.rs, which sit beside the component modules rather than inside them.

uuid.title: UUID
uuid.description: A UUID in the hyphenated form. SPEC §3 writes identities lowercase; a reader accepts either case, so this does too.

declared_entity_id.title: declared entity id
declared_entity_id.description: The identity of an entity somebody wrote down: a freshly minted UUID meaning nothing but "this one" (SPEC §3). This is the one identity in the format that is a real UUID.

derived_entity_id.title: derived entity id
derived_entity_id.description: The identity of an entity a generator produced: the address it was produced at — the declared generator's UUID, then the `/`-joined key that walks down to it, `6f1c…/instance:2/relay:1,0`. The address IS the identity, with nothing computed underneath it; two implementations name the same entity because they walked the same chain (SPEC §3). This is the flat spelling, which is what an `id` field and a database key hold; `derivation_address` below is the same address written in the two parts a record addresses one by.

entity_id.title: entity id
entity_id.description: The identity of one entity, either way it was minted: a UUID for a declared entity, a derivation address for a derived one. The two arms record HOW a name came about and never a kind of entity — derivation is a convenience and never a second class of existence (SPEC §1, §3) — so every field that names an entity takes either arm, and nothing may treat one differently once it has resolved it.

doc_id.title: document id
doc_id.description: The identity of one document, which is what `doc.depends_on` names.

local_handle.title: local handle
local_handle.description: A template-internal entity's name, standing in for an identity until a stamp mints one. `/` is forbidden inside it because `/` joins derivation key segments (SPEC §3).

local_ref.title: local reference
local_ref.description: How one template internal names another before either has an identity; expansion rewrites it to the stamped identity (SPEC §2). The handle stands alone, a `$comment` aside, as a parameter does: every reader rewrites exactly this shape, reads a `local_ref` beside a `key` as a local derivation address, and refuses one in any other company.

entity_ref.title: entity reference
entity_ref.description: A pointer at another entity: an identity out in the world — a declared entity's UUID or a derived entity's address, either is valid here — and, inside a template only, a local handle, or a parameter that the stamp replaces with the value it binds. A dangling one is a load error, never a best-effort match (SPEC §2, §6).

derivation_key.title: derivation key
derivation_key.description: The `/`-joined chain of segments naming one derived entity beneath its generator. Every segment is a nonempty opaque application-defined string. Only `/` (ancestry) and `@` (version pins) are reserved; all other spelling is preserved exactly (SPEC §3). Inside a template only, a parameter may stand for the whole key (SPEC §6).

derivation_segment.title: derivation segment
derivation_segment.description: One step of a derivation key: a nonempty opaque application-defined string. This is what a derived subtree keys its nodes by (SPEC §3, §8).

derivation_address.title: derivation address
derivation_address.description: The complete address of one derived entity, in the two parts a record writes it in: the declared generator the chain starts at, and the key that walks down from it. This is the same identity `derived_entity_id` spells flat, and a record addresses a derived entity by it (SPEC §3).

local_derivation_address.title: local derivation address
local_derivation_address.description: A derivation address written inside a template, where the generator is still a handle; expansion rewrites it into a plain derivation address (SPEC §3). The handle and the key stand alone, a `$comment` aside, as a bare `local_ref` does: every reader rewrites exactly this shape and refuses a `local_ref` in any other company.

cell_address.title: cell address
cell_address.description: How anything names one cell: by its own identity — a declared cell's UUID or a derived cell's address, the two being equally valid here — by that derived address written in its two parts, or, inside a template only, by a local one: a handle alone for a cell the template declares, a handle and a key for a cell one of its internals derives. A parameter may stand for any of these, inside a template only, and the stamp replaces it with the value it binds. Never a bare key string, which would only mean something to whichever entity coined it (SPEC §3, §6).

param_ref.title: parameter reference
param_ref.description: A template parameter standing where a value goes; substitution replaces the whole object with the bound value, preserving its JSON type (SPEC §6). Partial-string interpolation does not exist.

annotations.title: annotation keys
annotations.description: The `$`-prefixed keys a document may carry. `$comment` is ignored by every consumer everywhere, including inside maps whose other keys are data (SPEC §2). Referenced wherever the authoring profile closes an object, so a comment is never mistaken for a stray field.

steps.title: steps
steps.description: A length: an integer count of the steps of the frame it is stated in. Only the primary frame's `unit_mm` says what a step is worth, which is why no length field carries a unit in its name any more (SPEC §5).

steps_positive.title: positive steps
steps_positive.description: A length that must be greater than zero: an extent, a pitch, a footprint side.

unit_mm.title: step size in millimetres
unit_mm.description: What one integer step is worth physically — the only fractional number a geometry document carries, declared by the primary frame and by no other (SPEC §4, §5). 0.1 is the expected site default, because source drawings carry tenths of a millimetre and a tenth is finer than anything a warehouse holds to.

coord.title: coordinate
coord.description: One axis of a position, in the steps of the frame that states it (SPEC §5).

count.title: count
count.description: How many of something, zero included.

count_positive.title: positive count
count_positive.description: How many of something, where none of it would be meaningless.

flag.title: flag
flag.description: A yes-or-no fact about an entity.

steps_pair.title: step pair
steps_pair.description: Two lengths, x then y, in the steps of the frame that states them.

steps_pair_positive.title: positive step pair
steps_pair_positive.description: Two lengths that must both exceed zero: a size, a pitch, a footprint.

steps_list.title: step list
steps_list.description: Lengths in a stated order, as many as the thing has.

steps_pair_list.title: step pair list
steps_pair_list.description: Offsets in a stated order, each a pair of lengths in the steps of the frame that states them.

position.title: position
position.description: A point in a frame: two entries in a 2-D frame, three in a 3-D one (SPEC §4).

coord_pair.title: coordinate pair
coord_pair.description: Two coordinates in the frame of whatever states them, x then y.

axis_vector.title: axis vector
axis_vector.description: One number per axis of a frame — two entries, or three where a 2-D frame embeds in a 3-D parent and the third entry is its elevation (SPEC §4).
